title: Records, tax forms and professional help

sources.claim: Keep records that support income, deductions or credits until the period of limitations for that return runs out; generally 3 years, with longer periods in some situations.

sections.skill: Keep tax records for the right time and know when to get help

questions.prompt: What does the IRS say is the general period for keeping supporting records?

choices.text: 3 years, with longer periods in some situations
1 month, after which records can be thrown away
Forever, for every single receipt in every case
Only until the money is spent

questions.correct_answer: 3 years, with longer periods in some situations
questions.intro: Keep records that support income, deductions or credits until the period of limitations for that tax return runs out. The IRS says this is generally 3 years, with longer periods in some situations, such as certain errors or employment tax records. Keep receipts, invoices, bank statements, mileage logs and copies of filed returns, stored safely (for example, scanned with a backup). Tax forms depend on the business structure. Ask a tax professional when your situation is complex or you are unsure which forms apply.

sections.skill: A file box with labeled years

questions.prompt: Each folder in the box is for what?
questions.correct_answer: One year
questions.intro: Picture a file box with one folder for each year. Each folder holds that year's receipts, invoices, bank statements and a copy of the tax return. When a folder is old enough that the period for that return has passed (generally 3 years, sometimes longer), it may be cleared out. Until then, it stays. A scanned copy is like a spare box kept somewhere else, in case the first one is lost.
